messages.content:
Below are five AI-generated responses to the same task, labelled A through E.

Each response was written by one of these five language models:
GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek.

For each of the five responses, identify which model you believe wrote it, judging only from writing style, structure, and phrasing.

Answer independently for each response. Your five answers do not need to be five different models - name whichever model you believe wrote each response, even if that means naming the same model more than once.

Reply with JSON only, in exactly this form and nothing else:

{
  "A": {"model": "<one of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek>", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "<one short sentence>"},
  "B": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "C": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "D": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."},
  "E": {"model": "...", "confidence": <1-5>, "reason": "..."}
}

confidence: 1 = pure guess, 5 = certain.

--- RESPONSE A ---
Cooking meals at home is generally healthier than eating out most of the time because it gives you far more control over what you eat. When you prepare your own food, you decide how much salt, sugar, oil, and butter to use, and you can choose fresher ingredients such as vegetables, lean proteins, whole grains, and fruits. Restaurant meals often contain larger portions and hidden amounts of fat, sodium, and added sugar because they are designed to taste rich and appealing. At home, you can adjust recipes to fit your needs, avoid ingredients that do not agree with you, and make balanced meals that support better long-term health.

Home cooking is also cheaper, and that can make healthy eating easier to maintain. Eating out regularly adds up quickly, especially when drinks, tips, delivery fees, or service charges are included. With the same amount of money, a person can often buy ingredients for several meals at home. Saving money on food can make it more realistic to buy nutritious staples and plan meals ahead of time instead of relying on fast food or takeout when hungry. Because home cooking stretches the budget further, it supports a more consistent and healthier routine.

Cooking at home also builds useful life skills that improve a person’s relationship with food. Learning how to plan meals, read recipes, shop wisely, store ingredients, and prepare simple dishes makes people more independent and confident. These skills help them make better choices instead of depending on restaurants or convenience foods. Over time, cooking becomes easier and more enjoyable, and it encourages people to think about nutrition, portion sizes, and variety. For these reasons, preparing meals at home is usually a healthier habit than eating out most of the time.

--- RESPONSE B ---
Cooking meals at home is, in most cases, a healthier choice than regularly eating out, and the reasons for this extend well beyond the plate itself. When you prepare food in your own kitchen, you make countless small decisions that shape not only your physical well-being but also your finances and your personal development. Restaurants, by contrast, are designed to deliver flavor and convenience at scale, which often means that nutrition, cost, and skill-building take a back seat to speed and profit. Taking the time to cook for yourself most days of the week turns an ordinary necessity into an opportunity to look after your body, your wallet, and your capacity to care for yourself and others.

The most immediate benefit of home cooking is that you have complete control over what goes into your food. In a restaurant kitchen, dishes are often prepared with generous amounts of salt, butter, oil, and sugar because those ingredients make food taste richer and keep customers coming back. Portion sizes tend to be larger than what a person actually needs, and hidden additives, preservatives, and refined ingredients can appear even in meals that seem wholesome on the menu. When you cook at home, you choose the quality of the produce, the type of oil, the amount of salt, and the freshness of the proteins. You can adjust recipes to accommodate allergies, dietary goals, or simple preferences, and you know exactly what you are putting into your body. Over months and years, this level of control translates into meaningful differences in weight, energy, cholesterol, blood pressure, and overall health.

Beyond nutrition, cooking at home is significantly cheaper than eating out, and that financial advantage has its own health implications. A meal prepared from basic groceries typically costs a fraction of what the same dish would cost in a restaurant, where you are paying not only for ingredients but also for labor, rent, utilities, and profit margins. Buying staples like rice, beans, vegetables, and seasonal produce in bulk stretches a modest grocery budget across many meals, while a few restaurant visits each week can quietly consume hundreds of dollars a month. The money saved can be redirected toward higher-quality ingredients, regular medical care, gym memberships, or simply the peace of mind that comes with financial stability, all of which contribute to a healthier life in the broader sense.

Finally, cooking at home builds practical life skills that pay dividends for a lifetime. Learning to plan meals, shop efficiently, handle a knife, balance flavors, and manage the timing of multiple dishes develops a kind of everyday competence that few other activities offer. These skills grow with practice, and they make a person more self-reliant, more resourceful, and better equipped to feed family members, host friends, and adapt to changing circumstances. Someone who can cook is less dependent on takeout when money is tight, better able to recover from illness or stress through nourishing meals, and more likely to pass healthy habits on to children or roommates. Eating out occasionally remains one of life's genuine pleasures, but making home cooking the default rather than the exception is a quiet investment in health, savings, and self-sufficiency that compounds in value over the years.

--- RESPONSE C ---
In an era dominated by convenient food delivery apps and fast-food chains, the temptation to dine out has never been stronger. However, choosing to prepare meals at home most of the time remains one of the most beneficial decisions a person can make for their overall well-being. Transitioning from a lifestyle of frequent dining out to one centered around the home kitchen offers a multitude of advantages that extend far beyond simple physical health. By committing to home-cooked meals, individuals can dramatically improve their nutritional intake, secure their financial future, and foster personal growth through the acquisition of valuable practical abilities.

The most immediate health benefit of cooking at home is the absolute control it grants over the ingredients that enter the body. Restaurant meals, while often delicious, are engineered to maximize flavor at the expense of nutrition, typically by incorporating excessive amounts of sodium, refined sugars, and saturated fats. When preparing food in a personal kitchen, one becomes the ultimate gatekeeper of nutrition. It is possible to select fresh, whole ingredients, limit processed additives, and choose healthier cooking methods such as baking or steaming instead of deep-frying. Furthermore, portion sizes can be managed mindfully, preventing the overeating that frequently occurs when presented with the oversized platters typical of commercial dining establishments.

Beyond physical health, the financial benefits of home cooking contribute significantly to reducing mental stress and promoting financial wellness. Eating out carries a heavy premium, as consumers are not just paying for the food itself, but also for restaurant labor, overhead costs, and profit margins. In contrast, purchasing groceries in bulk and planning weekly meals allows for highly cost-effective eating. A single restaurant meal can often cost the same as a week's worth of home-cooked lunches. The money saved by avoiding daily restaurant bills and delivery fees can accumulate rapidly, allowing individuals to allocate those funds toward other life goals, such as savings, fitness memberships, or higher-quality ingredients that might otherwise seem unaffordable.

In addition to physical and financial health, the act of cooking serves as a powerful vehicle for personal development by building essential life skills. Navigating a kitchen requires and refines a diverse set of abilities, including time management, organization, and creative problem-solving. Learning how to balance flavors, handle kitchen tools safely, and plan meals around available ingredients fosters a sense of self-reliance and confidence. Over time, these culinary skills transform cooking from a chore into a rewarding form of self-expression and stress relief. This practical knowledge is a lifelong asset that can be passed down to future generations, ensuring that the tradition of healthy, independent living continues.

Ultimately, the choice to cook at home most of the time is a holistic investment in oneself. While the convenience of restaurants is undeniable for occasional indulgence, relying on them for daily sustenance compromises personal health, drains financial resources, and fosters dependency on others for basic survival needs. By taking charge of the kitchen, individuals reclaim power over what they consume, protect their hard-earned money, and cultivate a rich set of practical skills that enhance their quality of life. Embracing the home kitchen is not merely about feeding the body, but about nurturing a healthier, more mindful, and self-sufficient lifestyle.

--- RESPONSE D ---
Cooking meals at home tends to be healthier than eating out most of the time because it allows complete control over the ingredients that go into each dish, enabling choices that minimize excessive salt, sugar, unhealthy fats, and artificial additives commonly found in restaurant preparations while emphasizing fresh produce, lean proteins, and whole grains that support better nutrition and long-term well-being. This level of oversight also makes it easier to accommodate specific dietary needs or restrictions, reducing the risk of consuming hidden calories or allergens that can contribute to weight gain or other health issues over repeated outings. 

Beyond ingredient management, preparing food at home proves far more economical than frequent restaurant visits, freeing up resources that can be redirected toward higher-quality, nutrient-dense components like organic vegetables or specialty grains that might otherwise seem costly when dining out, thereby sustaining a pattern of healthier eating without financial strain. 

Finally, developing proficiency in the kitchen through regular home cooking cultivates essential life skills that encourage consistent meal preparation and informed decision-making about nutrition, fostering habits that promote sustained health benefits and independence from reliance on processed or convenience foods available elsewhere.

--- RESPONSE E ---
Cooking meals at home is undeniably healthier than eating out most of the time, primarily because it allows you to control exactly what goes into your food. When preparing meals at home, you have the power to choose fresh, high-quality ingredients and avoid excessive amounts of salt, sugar, unhealthy fats, and artificial additives that are often found in restaurant dishes. This level of control is particularly important for those managing dietary restrictions or health conditions, as it ensures meals align with specific nutritional needs. Additionally, home-cooked meals often involve simpler, more wholesome recipes, which can contribute to better overall health and well-being compared to the calorie-dense, nutrient-poor options frequently served in restaurants.

Another compelling reason to cook at home is that it is significantly cheaper than eating out regularly. Dining at restaurants or ordering takeout can quickly add up, especially when considering the costs of service charges, tips, and premium pricing for convenience. In contrast, cooking at home allows you to purchase ingredients in bulk, plan meals around seasonal produce, and minimize food waste, all of which contribute to substantial savings over time. This financial benefit not only makes healthy eating more accessible but also encourages a more sustainable approach to food consumption. By allocating the money saved toward other priorities, cooking at home becomes an economically savvy and health-conscious choice.

Beyond the immediate health and financial advantages, cooking at home also builds useful life skills that can have lasting benefits. Learning to prepare meals fosters independence, creativity, and a deeper understanding of nutrition, which can positively impact one’s lifestyle in the long term. It encourages mindfulness about food choices and promotes a sense of accomplishment and self-sufficiency. Moreover, cooking can be a social activity, bringing family and friends together to share meals and create meaningful connections. These skills are not only practical but also enriching, contributing to a more balanced and fulfilling life. In summary, cooking at home offers a trifecta of benefits: it ensures healthier meals, saves money, and cultivates valuable skills that extend far beyond the kitchen.

--- END OF RESPONSES ---
Now output the JSON object described above, and nothing else.
